subject: Encyclopedic VQA kickoff: retrieval-augmented visual QA
body:
Hi team,

Kicking off the Encyclopedic VQA effort. The dataset from our open-source release is the asset: 221k unique question+answer pairs about detailed properties of fine-grained categories, matched to images for 1M VQA samples, plus a controlled knowledge base derived from Wikipedia with evidence for every answer.

The product story writes itself from the published numbers: a state-of-the-art vision+language model gets only 13.0% accuracy on the single-hop single-answer part, while augmenting a large LM with knowledge-base retrieval reaches 48.8%. Retrieval is the product, not model scale.

Milestones (Apr 20 - Jul 20): eval harness on the single-hop split by May 15, our own retrieval-augmented baseline by June 12, launch review pre-read with a deployable-model plan by mid-July.

Daniela has staffing. One early flag: the knowledge base touches Wikipedia-derived content, so I'll start the privacy/licensing review conversation early given the 2-3 week SLA.

Priya
